summary: Edge-proxy strips x-redwood-roles header causing intermittent 403s for private VPC customers
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403 Forbidden responses for calls to the Redwood Private inference endpoint. Root cause appears to be an intermediary edge appliance in the customer's network path removing the x-redwood-roles header that our authz-service relies on for RBAC resolution.

Impact: Affects a subset of API calls from CarmenHealth production VPC; results in failed admin and service-account operations and user-facing errors when role-bearing requests are required. Approximately ~2-4% of requests in a 24h window returned 403 with no downstream error payload. Customer reports impact to nightly ingestion job and web console users.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed edge appliance -> customer firewall -> Redwood private ingress). Region: us-east. Customer tenants: carmen-prod.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run curl against private endpoint via customer network funnel (through customer's Citrix/bluecoat appliance used at edge).
2) Include a valid bearer token and x-redwood-roles: admin,ingest header.
3) Observe intermittent 403 responses (approx every ~25th request) with no change to token or request body.

Observed behavior: 403 Forbidden, authz-service logs show missing role claim (roles array empty). In ingress-proxy logs we see upstream request arrives with x-redwood-roles present but the request received by authz backend sometimes lacks the header.

Expected behavior: Header preserved end-to-end and authz evaluates roles successfully, returning 200 where permissions allow.

Relevant logs / traces:
- TraceID: 8f3a2c9a-7b1e-4c2f-9a2e-11b3b2f5c9d1 (example of successful request).
- TraceID: a4d2b7f1-2c3d-4e5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b (example of 403 where header missing).
- Ingress proxy capture (tcpdump) shows initial client packet includes header: x-redwood-roles: admin,ingest
- HTTP request at authz-service for failed trace shows no x-redwood-roles present.

Workaround: Customer can configure edge appliance to pass-through unknown headers or configure appliance header-whitelist to include x-redwood-roles. We provided temporary instructions and a suggested ACL change.

Request: Investigate whether our ingress-proxy can be made tolerant to missing headers by falling back to token-embedded role claims, and provide recommended configuration for customers using middleboxes that rewrite headers.

investigation:
Summary of findings: 1) Customer edge appliance is intermittently rewriting or stripping headers that contain the substring 'redwood' when the header payload includes multiple comma-separated roles. 2) Authz-service logic currently treats any presence of x-redwood-roles header (even if empty string) as authoritative and skips token-based fallback. 3) Ingress-proxy and our TLS termination do not introduce header loss in controlled tests; mismatch only occurs when simulating customer's appliance behavior.

Evidence and next steps: - Replayed captured pcap through controlled appliance and reproduced. - Created unit test to assert fallback behavior when header is empty or malformed. - Created PR to authz-service to treat empty or whitespace-only x-redwood-roles as absent (see related_github_prs). - SRE to propose ingress-proxy logging change to surface header-length and presence for quick debugging. - Recommend runbook update for private customers to include 'allow-list x-redwood-roles' for appliance whitelists.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: Provided CarmenHealth with appliance ACL change and explicit configuration snippet to whitelist x-redwood-roles; they applied and saw immediate reduction in failures.
Permanent fix: Authz-service patch merged to treat empty/whitespace x-redwood-roles as absent (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authz-service/pull/331). Patch deployed to private control plane canary on 2024-10-17; rollout plan: canary (10%), monitor 24h, full rollout if no regressions.
Follow-ups: - Update private-deploy runbook and onboarding checklist to include guidance on header-whitelisting for common middleboxes. - Add an automated check in our onboarding verifier that warns if edge path contains appliances known to rewrite headers. - Engineering story INT-3321 created to add ingress-proxy instrumentation for header-length and header-count metrics.
resolution_notes: Deployed authz patch and customer appliance config reduced incidents to baseline. Continue to monitor traces for 7 days. Customer success to schedule follow-up call to finalize long-term compliance configuration. Logged post-deployment metrics to console dashboard: authz.header_fallback_rate dropped from 3.7% -> 0.1%.
